column1: # Feature-level P4 evidence anchors for the P5 three-axis ledger (G2 closure).
# One row per `(feature_id, frontend)`: the hand-declared behaviour test that
# backs the shape's delivery claim for that feature.  The anchor must be a real
# nextest test id, exactly as `cargo nextest list` reports it; the resolver
# (scripts/parity/resolve_frontend_evidence.py) checks set membership (R4) and
# fails the run when a referenced test is renamed or deleted.
# Columns (TAB separated):
#   feature_id  stable `FeatureId` id; the vocabulary authority is the Rust
#               `FeatureId::ALL` registry in taskmanager-ui-contract (the
#               contract test rejects an unknown id, mirroring `ContractTag`).
#   frontend    gpui | iced | tui | bevy
#   test_id     the nextest test path, or `-` on a pending row
#   status      anchored | pending
#   note        `-` on an anchored row; the honest gap on a pending row
# Discipline (same as the facet manifest and the unified matrix):
#   * anchors are declared by hand and verified against discovery; a test id is
#     NEVER derived by scanning Rust source;
#   * `pending` is not a pass: it records that this `(feature, frontend)` pair
#     was surveyed and no discoverable behaviour test exists yet, so the folded
#     cell stays refused by G2 with this note as the recorded gap;
#   * a row absent from this table is simply not yet surveyed; `Ready` still
#     requires a committed anchor, so absence is never a silent delivery claim.
# First anchored batch (2026-09-22): the four features every frontend really
# renders and every Linux source lane registers as `Present` -
# `handles.enumeration`, `threads.topology`, `services.lifecycle-control`,
# `services.dependency-dag`.  The anchor proves the shape's delivered surface
# for that feature (the P1 semantic specification owns "what counts as
# delivered"; this table owns "a real test exists and resolves").
# Second anchored batch (2026-09-22, W14-A): eight further features whose
# delivered surface exists on the frontends listed below and whose whole
# `Requires` capability set is `Present` on the Linux source lane -
# `gpu.engine-utilization`, `memory.breakdown-rss-pss`,
# `storage.device-topology`, `services.inventory`,
# `security.posix-capabilities`, `security.sandbox-detection`,
# `hardware.heterogeneous-cores`, `hardware.core-frequency`.  Every anchor was
# hand-verified against the feature's semantic specification (the P1
# `delivery_definition`) and checked by membership in `cargo nextest list`.
# A frontend with no test proving the shape's delivered surface stays
# unanchored; a surveyed near-miss is recorded below as an explicit gap.
# Third anchored batch (2026-09-22, W15-A): six further cells whose whole
# `Requires` capability set is `Present` on the Linux source lane and whose
# delivered surface a real frame/panel test proves -
# `storage.smart-health` (iced/tui), `storage.iops-queue-latency` (tui),
# `power.battery-inventory` (iced/tui), and `services.log-stream` (iced).
# Every anchor was hand-verified clause by clause against that feature's
# `delivery_definition`: the receipt names the clauses each anchor proves and
# the clauses that stay unasserted.  The same survey re-read the remaining
# target features and records each real near-miss as an explicit `pending`
# row (swap-throughput rates, the remaining IOPS/queue/latency rows, the GPUI
# SMART/battery/log surfaces, the thermal-zone source traversal, the
# process-details fault and huge-page counters, and the Bevy namespace audit);
# a feature with no test touching its surface at all stays without a row.
# Fourth anchored batch (2026-09-22, W16-A): the GPUI cells whose
# `power.battery-inventory` / `power.thermal-zones` claims were previously
# recorded as pending on the strength of evidence that turned out to be
# test-tree-only. The GPUI System hardware page never rendered battery or
# thermal-control rows: `system_view/detail_rows.rs` defined its own
# `battery_detail_rows` / `thermal_control_rows` folds inside the test tree and
# the tests asserted those, while the i18n keys they used
# (`system.battery_power`, `system.battery_cycles`, `system.cooling`,
# `system.throttle`) had zero production references. That fixture and its five
# tests were deleted rather than rendered; the two real GPUI delivery surfaces
# now carry anchors - the Performance page's battery stat panel
# (`battery_stats`, charge/power/voltage/health/cycles with honest absence) and
# the System Health sensor center (`sensor_rows`, one labelled row per
# thermal-zone reading). `power.thermal-throttle-events` (the fake fixture's
# other half) was declared `Unsupported` by this shape then and gained no row;
# the W25-A batch at the end of this file later delivered and anchored it.
# Fifth anchored batch (2026-09-22, W16-B/W16-C): eighteen new anchored rows
# plus one re-verified row, each hand-checked clause by clause against the
# feature's `delivery_definition` and each test id checked by membership in
# `cargo nextest list` before it was committed.  W16-B closed the TUI
# observation gaps: the Properties-modal page-fault counters (minor + major on
# one painted row, honest dash when unobserved), the details-panel anonymous
# huge-page charge (value + RSS share, never a fabricated 0 B), the painted
# service log stream with its level filter reaching the drawn rows, and the
# disk panel's queue/service row.  The already-anchored
# `storage.iops-queue-latency` TUI row is the re-verified one: the same frame
# test now writes the queue/service pair explicitly and proves all three
# definition clauses in one frame - IOPS 137, latency 1.50 ms, queue depth
# 2.50 - and omits the row when the pair is unobserved.  W16-C closed the
# Iced/Bevy observations: the swap-in/out throughput rates, the
# IOPS/response/queue/service rows, the PageFaults/AnonHugePages counters, the
# per-adapter GPU enumeration (Iced and Bevy) with Bevy's per-engine rows, the
# Bevy partition rows and the six-family Bevy SMART evidence (availability,
# temperature, percentage used, available spare, power-on hours, unsafe
# shutdowns), the Bevy painted log stream under its level filter, and the Bevy
# Linux namespace audit (per-kind host/isolated status).  Five cells had no row
# before and are newly surveyed (Iced `gpu.adapter-enumeration`; Bevy
# `storage.iops-queue-latency`, `gpu.adapter-enumeration`,
# `memory.page-faults`, `memory.transparent-huge-pages`); the other thirteen
# replace a surveyed `pending` row with the verified anchor.  An anchored row
# still carries `-` in the note column by schema, so the batch clause record
# lives here.  The remaining `pending` rows keep their honest gaps: no test
# proves the shape's delivered surface for them yet.
# Follow-up in the same batch (2026-09-22, W17-A): the Iced
# `power.thermal-zones` cell was converted from `pending` to anchored after
# the Iced health line landed the real delivery surface (the health modal's
# thermal-zone panel).  The anchor is the traversal test - one row per shared
# sensor-center temperature reading, each named by the reading's own source
# label, with a failed read kept as the shared dash and never a fabricated
# `0.0 °C`.  The same module's panel test proves the painted panel appears for
# a temperature channel and stays absent for a fan-only snapshot, and its
# capture-fixture test only seeds a named zone for the evidence run; those two
# are supporting evidence, not the anchor.  Together with the eighteen rows
# above the batch now carries nineteen anchors, and no `pending` row remains
# on any shape whose delivered surface a real test proves.
# Sixth anchored batch (2026-09-22, W18-A): the six GPUI cells that the W15-A
# and W16-B/W16-C surveys left as explicit `pending` gaps.  Each anchor was
# hand-checked clause by clause against the feature's `delivery_definition`
# and its test id confirmed by membership in
# `cargo nextest list -p taskmanager-gpui --features test-support`.
# `services.inventory` is anchored on the painted inventory frame: one row per
# projected unit, each carrying a status cell whose test-support selector
# spells the same typed `ServiceStatus` token the cell paints, and the typed
# status filter is the painted membership authority (only the matching unit
# reaches the frame; an empty match paints no placeholder row).
# `storage.device-topology` is anchored on the disk page's painted partition
# rows: the mounted partitions paint identity/usage/bar slots whose fill width
# is the observed used/total fraction (40% and 80%), the unmounted unit stays
# as the compact summary line instead of a fabricated row, and a partition
# without observations paints no fill at all (never a 0% bar).
# `storage.smart-health` is anchored on the production `disk_stats` row fold:
# reported availability, the shared temperature readout with its critical
# bound, every per-sensor temperature, percentage used, available spare with
# its warning threshold, power-on hours, and unsafe shutdowns each carry the
# real projected value, while a provider without SMART telemetry grows none of
# those rows and never a fabricated `0%`/`0 h`/`0`.
# `storage.swap-throughput` is anchored on the Memory page's production stat
# fold: the observed swap-in (2.0 MiB/s) and swap-out (512.0 KiB/s) rates each
# render their own row (the swap used/total occupancy row is a separate fact),
# and an unobserved or typed-unavailable rate leaves no row at all.
# `storage.iops-queue-latency` is anchored on the same disk fold: observed
# IOPS 137, response 1.54 ms, average queue depth 2.25, and the separate
# service-time estimate 0.42 ms each reach their row, while a first-sample gap
# keeps the row's value as the shared dash.
# `services.log-stream` is anchored on the painted service-details dialog: an
# accepted batch paints one row per projected entry, and advancing the painted
# level control (All -> Errors) before the next batch leaves only the error row
# painted; a cold or rejected stream paints the typed state and no fabricated
# row.  Two GPUI observation limits are recorded here: the harness exposes
# geometry per debug selector (no text readback), so the inventory status-cell
# selector derives its token from the same typed `ServiceStatus` the cell
# paints; and a `debug_bounds` entry survives the frame that painted it, so the
# states that must be absent are asserted on a fresh window (never as an
# in-window disappearance).
# Follow-up in the same batch (2026-09-22, W18-A): the TUI
# `storage.swap-throughput` cell was converted from `pending` to anchored after
# the TUI line landed its painted-frame test.  The anchor seeds both rates
# through the canonical `MemoryScalarObservations` group the Linux provider
# fills (`swap_in_bytes_per_sec` / `swap_out_bytes_per_sec`) and asserts the
# painted frame carries `Swap in 2.0 MiB/s` and `Swap out 512.0 KiB/s`; a
# `TimedOut` observation keeps both labelled rows on the shared dash and the
# test explicitly rejects a fabricated `Swap in 0 B` / `Swap out 0 B`.  The
# production rows are the TUI memory stats' typed
# `current_swap_in/out_bytes_per_sec` readouts, which keep the labelled shared
# dash when the observation is absent.  The same batch's sibling honesty test
# (`memory_stats_rows_render_honest_dashes_when_unavailable`) covers the
# never-observed demo case.  With this row the sixth batch carries seven
# anchors.
# Closing follow-up (2026-09-22, W20 tail): the last surveyed gap - the TUI
# `power.thermal-zones` cell - was converted to anchored after the TUI line
# landed the Fan page's SYSTEM thermal-zone group (the perf fan projection's
# `thermal_zone_lines`: every shared `Temperature` reading, each named by its
# own source label, an unread channel kept as the shared dash and never a
# fabricated `0.0 °C`).  The anchor is the painted Fan-page traversal test:
# one row per temperature reading - including a foreign-device zone the
# device-level fan context cannot reach - each named by the reading's own
# label, the unread zone kept as a named dash, and the frame asserted to carry
# no fabricated `0.0 °C`.  Its sibling tests prove the whole-group admission
# (a partial zone group is never painted) and the fanless reachability of the
# same surface; those are supporting evidence, not the anchor.  The committed
# table now carries 66 anchored rows and no surveyed gap.  The fold itself is
# unchanged: an anchor attaches only where the feature's whole `Requires` set
# is `Present` on the platform axis, so this table documents evidence and
# never forces a `Ready` cell; a future surveyed near-miss must again be
# committed as an explicit `pending` row.
# W23-A batch (2026-09-23): the `memory.breakdown-rss-pss` sweep.
# The P1 definition was narrowed to the facets the shared projection really
# delivers (resident RSS, proportional PSS, private/unique USS, and the
# derived-shared `RSS - USS` share); the virtual address-space size is
# explicitly OUTSIDE it (no `VmSize` observation exists) and the per-process
# swap charge stays a separate fact.  The application VM gained
# `ProcessDetailsField::Shared` and all four details surfaces now paint it, so
# every anchor proves the complete narrowed definition: the GPUI row was
# re-pointed from the gates-package table projection to the in-crate details
# dialog fold (`gpui_app::root::chrome::tests`), which proves the resident
# performance current plus the PSS/USS/derived-shared overview rows and the
# honest dash when the private facet is unobserved; the Iced and TUI anchors
# gained the same derived-shared value and cold-dash clauses; and the Bevy
# cell (previously surveyed but unanchored) gained its first anchor on the
# details-overview fold, taking the table to 67 anchored rows (bevy 16).

# W25-A batch (2026-09-23): the `power.thermal-throttle-events` sweep.  The
# W23-A definition had already been narrowed to the cumulative trigger
# counters (`package_throttle_count`/`core_throttle_count` of the shared CPU
# projection), with the real-time PROCHOT `is_throttled` state explicitly
# OUTSIDE it, and W24-A made `CpuPackageMetrics` their single authority plus
# the `telemetry.cpu.throttle` lane `Present` on Linux (registered-pending on
# Windows/macOS).  All four shapes now really render the counters on their CPU
# details surfaces, so the cell moves from the declared `Unsupported` gap to
# the honest delivery status (GPUI `Reference`, Iced/TUI/Bevy `Ported`) and
# each shape anchors the complete narrowed definition: one `S{package_id}`
# segment per package that observed at least one counter, both the package
# and the per-core event count painted from the shared projection, the
# unobserved-family honest absence (GPUI/Iced/TUI omit the row; Bevy's
# always-mounted diagnostic row keeps the shared dash), and the labeled dash
# for an unobserved sibling counter — never a fabricated `0`.  The PROCHOT
# clause stays unasserted because it is outside the definition; the Linux
# `telemetry.cpu.throttle` lane keeps the whole cell host-derived.  This takes
# the table to 71 anchored rows (gpui 16, iced 18, tui 20, bevy 17).
